gaps.sentence: 'They were arguing all through dinner,' he said. He said they ___ arguing all through dinner.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: were arguing → had been arguing.

gaps.sentence: 'I work from home on Fridays,' he explained. He explained that he ___ from home on Fridays.
gaps.explanation: After a past reporting verb, present simple backshifts to past simple: work → worked.

gaps.sentence: 'OK, I'll help you move house,' she said. She ___ to help me move house.
gaps.explanation: Agreement to a request is reported as agreed to do something.

gaps.sentence: She ___ me not to worry about the deadline.
gaps.hint: tell sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: Only 'tell' takes a personal object + not to + infinitive; 'said me not to' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
gaps.explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll have finished by noon,' she promised. She promised she ___ finished by noon.
gaps.explanation: will have + past participle becomes would have + past participle.

gaps.sentence: 'It was me who ate the last biscuit,' the boy admitted. The boy ___ eating the last biscuit.
gaps.explanation: Admit takes a gerund (admit doing) or admit that + clause — never admit to do.
